findings.title: Host's Lua tick grew 4x over the run (16 -> 30 -> 59 ms); the joiners' only doubled
findings.evidence: All 95 perf lines (5-minute windows), averaged by phase, ms a tick (avg / first half / worst half). HOST Saint Alessia: r1-12 15.7 / 8.0 / 382; r13-20 29.5 / 16.3 / 750; r21-31 59.4 / 33.8 / 461. Samples: 18:49:03 'tick avg 10.4 ms (halves 4.7 + 5.6), worst half 169.0'; 19:29:58 35.3 (18.7 + 16.6); 20:01:27 69.1 (38.3 + 30.9), worst 338; 20:23:10 117.2 (81.9 + 35.2), worst 419. JOINERS, same three phases: Shazzy 5.0 / 6.4 / 9.0 (late 20:33:08 7.6 = 2.8 + 4.8); cressendo 7.9 / 10.4 / 14.2; dukka 3.7 / 6.0 / 10.8. Joiners' worst halves stayed at 79-261 ms. The host's worst halves were 270-461 ms in every window from r17 on, with 'rounds' the worst part (275, 271, 285, 359, 448, 305, 304, 363, 309, 294, 292, 316). Before that they were 118-172. Baselines: Alyssa solo 0.73.78 r1 24.3 ms (19.8 + 4.5). The 0.73.70 co-op hosts ran 67-118 ms, so from r21 this host is back in that range. The players felt it at the same time: host 'stuttering around wave 20-25', Shazzy 'Very noticeable by round 22', dukka 'round 23 or 24'.
findings.cause: Most of the growth is one native call, SV_UnitAlive, whose cost per call rises (next finding), plus the airfield music-hold walk and the leftover Spaceport turret watch (findings below). Survival's Lua lists are not the cause: the Lua heap stays at 5-15 MB with no trend.
findings.fix: Fix SV_UnitAlive's per-call cost and its per-second loops first (findings 2-3), then the music-hold walk (finding 5). Retest with the same perf lines. Target: host under ~20 ms average and worst half under 100 ms through round 30.

The host's Lua tick average went from 10-20 ms (18:49-19:14) to 44-117 ms (19:56-20:38), and its 'coop' part from 2.4 to 13.5 ms a tick. This matches the players' 'noticeable by round 22'.
findings.cause: Proven in code: runtime/coop.c:1370 sends the E states only from the per-frame CoStep, when now - lastEntSend >= 1/15 s, then sets lastEntSend = now. Each state interval is therefore a whole number of host frames of at least 66.7 ms, and one long frame pushes it past 120 ms. On the joiner, CoTrackOffset/CoAdaptDelay (coop.c:786-805) adapt the delay only to network lateness against the fastest arrival, not to the sender's gaps between states, so the delay stays at CO.delay 120 ms. Every gap longer than that is drawn by CoSample's extrapolation (coop.c:1266-1274) and then corrected. Inferred: the corrections are the 'gun kills very hard' (a gun solution against a copy that jumps 10-20 m). Late-round health x1.45 ('late: round 24 enemies' health x1.45') adds to it but isn't desync.
findings.fix: (1) Joiner: track each sender's 95th-percentile interval between E sender timestamps and set the delay to that + jitter + 30 ms (bounded), and log it in the minute line ('state gaps p95 N ms'). (2) Host: schedule E with lastEntSend += 1/15, clamped so it can't fall behind, or send every frame when the frame time exceeds 50 ms. At 25 fps that doubles E to ~25 packets/s per joiner, which fits easily: today it's ~32 packets/s and 6-9 KB/s in total. (3) Cut the host's per-frame cost: the perf area's 10 → 117 ms tick growth; the TESTER host also ran the weapons log and audit.

findings.evidence: cressendo's lines: rtt 266-336 ms (host's view), lateness 47-64 ms in rounds 1-19, then spikes to 394 ms (r20), 424 (r23), 410 (r24) and 315 (r26), with 'drawn 300 ms' (the cap) or 214-224 ms. verify.note: The figures are right but the conclusion is not. cressendo's draw delay was 120 ms (CO.delay) in almost every minute, with lateness 44-108 ms. The 300 ms cap was reached only in four minute lines (host 19:44 L394, 20:02 L424, 20:07 L410, 20:16 L315), plus 185-224 ms in three Spaceport minutes. Yet he was 8-12% past the newest state all run (round 2 already 8.9%; rounds 21 / 27 at 15.4 / 17.2%). His ~285 ms rtt is absorbed by the clock offset (offset = fastest one-way time); only lateness above that counts. With jit ~50 ms, CoAdaptDelay's want = jit + 30 = ~80 ms is clamped up to 120 ms. State gaps of 67-130 ms plus ~50 ms lateness then run past 120 ms much more often than for Shazzy or dukka (~20 ms lateness). So it is the same formula fault as finding 2 (the delay ignores the sender's state gap), not the cap. The '3 176/146 ms' line on Shazzy is from the Spaceport spike; other minutes show cressendo's stream at '120/55-59 ms'.
verify.fix: Use finding 2's joiner fix: delay = max(CO.delay, jit + p95 state gap + margin). For cressendo that is ~180-200 ms, well under the current 300 ms cap. Make the cap per sender (e.g. min(rtt/2 + p95 gap + 50 ms, 0.6 s)) only so that lateness spikes above 270 ms still fit. The migration ranking already penalises high rtt.

findings.cause: sv_coop.lua:4483-4484 sets M.storeKeep = want even when SV_StoreKeepAI returned a negative error, so the next tick sees want == M.storeKeep and never asks again. findings.fix: Record M.storeKeep only when old >= 0, so it is retried each tick until the runtime is ready. Use once() only for the log line.
